episodes.181786: Severe thunderstorms produced severe downburst winds and quarter sized hail the afternoon of 10 August 2023 across the southern Nebraska Panhandle.
episodes.181797: Two rounds of thunderstorms impacted Middle Tennessee on August 9-10, 2023. The first round of thunderstorms moved into the area during the early afternoon hours of August 9th with the strongest thunderstorms favoring areas south of Interstate 40. This activity was responsible for downing a few trees in Lawrence County. The second round of thunderstorms impacted Middle Tennessee late on August 9th and into the early morning hours of the 10th with a couple more fallen trees reported. Despite an unseasonable amount of wind shear, the atmosphere was likely too stable to produce widespread severe thunderstorms.
episodes.181852: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms raced east-southeast from the Ozarks through the mid South during the evening hours of the 9th and into the Tennessee Valley during the early morning hours of the 10th.  The line produced several reports of wind damage and one EF-0 tornado in Limestone County.
episodes.181965: A few showers and thunderstorms produced sporadic gale-force wind gusts.
episodes.182102: The air flow over Arizona slowly transitioned from a west to east trajectory, to more southerly. This was due to a nearly stationary low forming off the western coast of California, which will provided some dynamical forcing. This allowed moisture to move northward from Mexico. Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms formed over the north-central Arizona.
episodes.182631: Isolated, heat of the afternoon thunderstorms developed across portions of north central and northeast South Dakota. There were a few reports of severe wind gusts, with some localized wind related storm damage.
episodes.182633: A cold front brought the threat of severe thunderstorms to northeast South Dakota on the afternoon and evening of August 10th. Initially, individual storms presented both a hail and wind threat in the James Valley, with reports of golfball sized hail in Brown and Hand counties. As the storms moved east into the Prairie Coteau region, they organized into a broken line and presented more of a wind threat. The Department of Transportation mesonet station 6 miles west of Henry recorded a 74 mph wind gust, and the nearby town of Henry also experienced damage to trees. There was also a pair of brief tornado touchdowns farther to the south associated with one of the stronger cells embedded within this line, though no damage was ever noted.
episodes.182938: Numerous thunderstorms developed across the far northeastern Permian Basin along a late-season dryline setup. Very dry low-level conditions resulted in strong to severe downburst winds with a few of these thunderstorms.
episodes.183052: A supercell thunderstorm produced a swath of severe weather across portions of south central Nebraska during the evening of August 10th. A weak upper level disturbance and associated surface front/trough sparked isolated thunderstorms in Dawson and Buffalo Counties between 4-5 PM CDT. These storms developed amidst warm surface temperatures (near 90 degrees) and strong instability (CAPE values near 2000 J/kg). The strong instability and adequate deep layer shear allowed the isolated storms to morph into a singular, dominant supercell that tracked from the Kearney area at around 5 PM, southeastward towards Superior by around 9 PM. Large hail was the primary severe threat, with several instances of significant severe hail (at least 2 inches in diameter) reported along its path. As a result, the main impact from this severe event was crop damage, though vehicle and home damage also occurred. The storm exited Nebraska altogether between 9-10 PM CDT.
episodes.183093: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts along the southern Brevard County coast.
episodes.183146: Early on the morning of the 9th, a severe thunderstorm, developing in the wake of a previous convective line (see 8 August entry), lead to reports of wind damage and sub-severe hail across the western and northern fringes of the Lawton, Oklahoma community. ||By the evening, the combination of very hot temperatures and an approaching upper system lead to scattered development of high-based thunderstorms across southern Oklahoma. Sufficient downdraft potential energy (DCAPE) existed for damaging downbursts to be observed across the eastern Red River Valley.
episodes.183219: Plentiful low-level moisture and warm temperatures provided an ideal environment for showers and thunderstorms to develop along the Atlantic sea breeze boundary on August 10th. There was scattered thunderstorm activity across the interior, especially in southeastern Florida.
episodes.183418: Highly anomalous low level jet associated with a strong upper level shortwave brought an early morning thunderstorm complex through Tennessee, with flash flooding around Knoxville and damaging straight line winds in the southernmost counties.
episodes.183691: Severe thunderstorms developed into the afternoon and evening as a frontal zone settled southward across SE GA and an impulse moved across the front. Significant heat and surface moisture in addition to steepening lapse rates ahead of the mid-level impulse created volatile surface-based instability which supported severe downbursts/outflows (50-70 mph) and hail. Given the near alignment of steering flow and the initiating boundary, the potential for waves or training convection created a flood threat as well.
episodes.184043: Thunderstorms which developed in the afternoon across Central Alabama moved into West Central GA. One cell lasted for a significant amount of time along a shear boundary and lasted past midnight on the 10th. Isolated severe winds were the main hazard.
episodes.184065: A line of thunderstorms developed along a pre frontal surface trough during the afternoon. These storms briefly became severe with damaging winds and large hail observed as they crossed western portions of the Niagara Frontier. The storms then weakened as they pushed across the rest of western New York late in the afternoon.
episodes.184142: A strong storm system and associated cold front moved around the periphery of a high pressure system situated over the Gulf of Mexico. The boundary triggered scattered severe thunderstorms in northern Arkansas during the night-time hours bringing to large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding.
episodes.184604: An isolated severe storm developed across western Nebraska and moved across the southern Sandhills with damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.184628: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.184655: Severe thunderstorms produced intense straight-line winds over portions of Larimer and Weld counties.  Peak gusts ranged from 63 mph to 80 mph.
episodes.184685: Thunderstorms developed and moved through Eastern NC during the early evening hours. A few storms became severe and produced damaging wind gusts. In addition, a lightning strike cause major structural damage to a home in Duck.
episodes.184749: An upper level disturbance brought straight-line winds to the area. Convection intensified as it approached the coast with the early destabilization.
episodes.184889: A cold front pushed into the Mid-South during the late evening hours of August 9, 2023, and continued to push across the area during the early morning hours of August 10, 2023. Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across the  Mid-South.  The airmass across the region was moderately unstable with surface base convective available potential energy values of 2000 J/kg and 0-6 km bulk shear values that topped 50 knots. These parameters supported some organized severe weather resulting in few reports of large hail and damaging winds.

episodes.184967: After a broad area of rain moved through the region earlier in the day, a boundary sagged slowly south through the Ozarks. This boundary became the focus for  rounds of rain and storms. With ample instability available and a strong low level jet, storms were able to produce measured winds as high as 76 mph at times. With storms moving across the same locations thanks to the slow moving boundary, flooding also occurred for some locations.
episodes.184981: During the afternoon hours, a thunderstorm developed over Decatur County and moved into Norton County where it produced quarter sized hail near the town of Almena, Kansas.

episodes.185092: An active northwest upper flow pattern continued across the Central Gulf Coast region, producing severe weather mainly across the northern and eastern portions of Central Alabama.
episodes.185198: A weak surface front moved through NJ, sparking off a few showers and thunderstorms. Thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and two tornadoes in parts of New Jersey.
episodes.185214: A weak low-top supercell brought rain and winds, but no lightning to Fleming County during the early morning hours of August 10, 2023. However, within this system, a weak tornado developed and tracked across portions of the county. By daybreak, dispatch and emergency management began receiving reports of damage that had |occurred in the Beechburg community just east of Flemingsburg. Radar did show some weak rotation that moved across this location. After an NWS Damage Survey, it was determined that an EF-0 tornado had touched down, starting near the intersection of |Beechburg Road and Colgan Road, and continued about a third of a mile down Colgan Road before dissipating. Based on the path of damage, it is also likely that this tornado only lasted about a minute, and skipped a few times along it's track before |dissipating.
episodes.185271: A late day frontal zone moved into an unstable airmass with up to 2000 J/kg MUCAPE and sparked several severe thunderstorms, which produced large hail up to golf ball size. In addition, a couple of brief tornadic spin ups occurred across Kingsbury County, but resulted in no damage.
episodes.185360: An advancing cold front led to numerous showers and embedded thunderstorms tracking east during the morning and early afternoon hours. A few storms became severe in Anson and Sampson Counties.
episodes.185373: A line of thunderstorms moved across upstate South Carolina during the morning. Embedded storms produced brief strong-to-damaging wind gusts.
episodes.186587: Several gale-force peak convective wind gusts impacted the OH and PA shore of Lake Erie on August 6th and 10th. During the early afternoon through early evening of the 6th, a surface low drifted northeastward from northwestern OH to Lake St. Clair. The low became occluded as the trailing cold front moved eastward from far-western OH to central OH and a nearly-stationary front lingered near the Lake Erie shore in north-central and northeast OH. Isolated to scattered multicell thunderstorms persisted generally northeastward across far-northern OH and Lake Erie during the late afternoon through early evening after developing along the occluded and nearly-stationary fronts. These storms occurred along a tight gradient of MUCAPE and in a region of weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate effective bulk shear.  ||Several days later, a cold front drifted generally southward across southern ON and southern Lower MI to northern Lake Erie during the early afternoon through early evening of the 10th. Isolated to scattered multicell showers and thunderstorms persisted generally southeastward across Lake Erie after developing along the front. The storms persisted amidst weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate to strong effective bulk shear.

Damage was consistent with a high-end EF-0 tornado with maximum winds of 85 mph. The tornado was on the ground for approximately 7 minutes and had a maximum width of 225 yards.  Damage indicators were a mix of softwood and hardwood trees, uprooted or partially snapped along the path. The tornado formed on the northern shore of Wheeler Lake on Little Elk Road, downing softwood trees at this location. The tornado crossed Snake Road to the southeast, downing and uprooting additional softwood trees along Bay Hill and Bay Shore Drives. Several homes at this location sustained significant damage to docks as trees fell on them, with uprooted trees causing damage as well to retaining walls and sprinkler systems in this area. At this point, the tornado crossed the open waters along the north shore of Wheeler Lake before coming ashore again just before Davis Road. Several trees were uprooted along with very large, snapped branches here. One home sustained damage in this area as a tree fell on the back side of the structure. While the tree looked snapped, the health of the tree looked to be in question which likely led to its quick failure. The tornado then crossed an inlet and uprooted several more trees along Beechwood Road, before continuing to the Brigadoon neighborhood. Significant and more widespread tree damage was noted in this neighborhood as trees were uprooted, power poles knocked down, and large branches snapped. The tornado continued to follow the northern shore of Wheeler Lake but began weakening. Damage, much less widespread compared to areas further west, was observed along Beech Fork Lane and sporadic tree damage through Shaw Road. The tornado dissipated just east of Shaw Road.
